topic: Someone finds their college application essay published as an example
text:
Person: I just received an email stating that a draft of my personal statement for my college applications has been published online as a sample essay. My word count is way off and my name is in there, so I'm terrified they've stolen my work.

AI: That is an extremely stressful situation, but don't panic yet. First, we need to verify the context of the publication. Many schools and admissions consultants are legally required to publish sample essays on their websites to illustrate the format or offer writing tips, often without the author's specific name attached or with full permission granted upfront. Check if the publication came from your specific university's admissions department or a known educational resource.

Person: It was published on the official blog of the university I applied to as part of their "Student Voices" series. I didn't check the metadata on the page because I've been so focused on my own application deadlines. Should I contact them immediately to demand an apology and removal?
